BOOK ONE · LESSON 129

Seventy miles an hour 时速70英里

时速70英里

A dialogue lesson in which a policeman stops a man named Gary for driving too fast. The story introduces the modal verbs for past deduction 'must have been driving' (past continuous) and 'can't have been', and the structure 'you'd better (not) do something' for strong advice. The dialogue runs through Ann warning Gary to drive slowly, the policeman stopping him, Gary claiming he can't have been driving that fast, and the policeman warning him not to do it again. The workbook drills comprehension of the dialogue and vocabulary fill-in; the grammar workbook completes sentences with 'must have' or 'can't have' past forms, agrees with 'you'd better' advice, and completes advice with 'had better'.

READ & UNDERSTAND

Lesson 课文

Listen to the tape then answer this question. What does Ann advise her husband to do next time? 听录音，然后回答问题。安建议她的丈夫下次做什么？

听录音，然后回答问题。安建议她的丈夫下次做什么？

  1. 1

    ANN

    Look, Gary! That policeman's waving to you. He wants you to stop.

    瞧，加里！那个警察正朝你挥手呢。他要你停下来。

  2. 2

    POLICEMAN

    Where do you think you are? On a race track? You must have been driving at seventy miles an hour.

    你认为你现在是在哪儿？在赛车道上吗？你刚才一定是以每小时70英里的速度开车。

  3. 3

    GARY

    I can't have been.

    我不会开得那样快的。

  4. 4

    POLICEMAN

    I was doing eighty when I overtook you.

    我是以每小时80英里的速度赶上你的。

  5. 5

    POLICEMAN

    Didn't you see the speed limit?

    难道你没看见限速牌吗？

  6. 6

    GARY

    I'm afraid I didn't, officer. I must have been dreaming.

    恐怕我没有看见，警官。我一定是思想开小差了。

  7. 7

    ANN

    He wasn't dreaming, officer. I was telling him to drive slowly.

    警官，他思想没有开小差。我刚才正告诉他开慢点。

  8. 8

    GARY

    That's why I didn't see the sign.

    所以我才没看见那牌子。

  9. 9

    POLICEMAN

    Let me see your driving licence.

    让我看一看你的驾驶执照。

  10. 10

    POLICEMAN

    I won't charge you this time. But you'd better not do it again!

    这次我就不罚你款了。但你最好不要开再这样快。

  11. 11

    GARY

    Thank you. I'll certainly be more careful.

    谢谢您。我以后一定会多加注意。

  12. 12

    ANN

    I told you to drive slowly, Gary.

    加里，我刚才叫你开慢点吧。

  13. 13

    GARY

    You always tell me to drive slowly, darling.

    你总是叫我开慢点，亲爱的。

  14. 14

    ANN

    Well, next time you'd better take my advice!

    好啦，下次你最好还是听从我的劝告吧！

Notes on the text 课文注释

1. Where do you think you are?

do you think 是用在特殊疑问句中的插入语，用来征询见解或表达看法。

2. must have been driving

这种结构用来表示对过去正在进行的事情的推测。可译为「一定」或「准是」。

3. at seventy miles an hour

每小时70英里的速度。

4. I was doing eighty when I overtook you.

其中的动词 do 表示「以……速度行进」。

5. But you'd better not do it again!

you'd better = you had better，后面加动词原形。had better 用于建议在将来某一具体场合采取动作，而不用於一般情况，比 should 语气更为强烈，常有威胁、告诫或催促的意味。

6. you'd better take my advice!

你最好还是听从我的劝告。take one's advice 是「听从劝告」的意思。
